headline: Intel chief executive Lip-Bu Tan said Chinese AI models such as DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM are "good enough" and cost less per token.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: Tan spoke on Monday 12 October, before the window; opinion, with Intel's stock reaction as the market angle.
importance_line: Cheaper models could widen AI use and so the demand for chips and servers, which matters to chipmakers and AI buyers, but it also helps Chinese developers, and Tan did not set out any policy.
summary: Stocktwits reports, citing Reuters, that Lip-Bu Tan, chief executive of the chipmaker Intel, said on Monday 12 October that Chinese frontier models cost less per token and have been adopted "very fast," and that "I'm a strong believer of open source; that's the best way to drive efficiency." The article says his view echoes Jensen Huang, chief executive of Nvidia, who said in July that models from DeepSeek, Alibaba and Moonshot AI were "excellent."
notes: Reuters original not read; Stocktwits relays it. Date taken from 'on Monday' in a report published 15 Oct 00:30 UTC.
